sections.content: How many people stayed in Bolton-le-Sands after gaining qualifications?

Bolton-le-Sands is a small town in the North West. Bolton-le-Sands does not have its own university.

Bolton-le-Sands has lower levels of deprivation.

Overall, Bolton-le-Sands ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 310 state-school pupils from Bolton-le-Sands who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 145 (47%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 115 (37%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Bolton-le-Sands to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Bolton-le-Sands' pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Bolton-le-Sands in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Bolton-le-Sands move to?

Of Bolton-le-Sands's graduates, 80 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 25 of those graduates (31%) were living fairly locally, in the Lancaster and Morecambe travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Bolton-le-Sands's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 50 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 30 of those qualified non-graduates (60%) were living fairly locally, in the Lancaster and Morecambe travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Bolton-le-Sands' GCSE cohort:

  • 40 graduates left the North West

In 2018 to 2019, 33% of graduates living in Bolton-le-Sands had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 90 graduates from our cohort living in Bolton-le-Sands, compared with the 145 graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, 72% of graduates had sat their GCSEs in Bolton-le-Sands, while 33% had moved there from elsewhere.
